title: An LRU cache for the results page

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for an lru cache for the results page, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: On result day the college website falls over, because every student asks for the same few pages. Build the cache that sits in front of it: a fixed number of entries, O(1) get and put, and the least recently used entry thrown out when space runs out. This is the classic list-plus-hash-map design that interviews ask about, built and tested end to end.
requirements: CAP sets the capacity once (1 to 9999).
GET returns the value or 'miss'; a hit makes the key the most recently used.
PUT inserts or updates and makes the key the most recently used; when full, the least recently used key is evicted and named.
KEYS lists keys from most to least recently used; STATS counts hits and misses.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `CAP <n>` | `cache of <n>` |
| `PUT <key> <value>` | `stored <key>` or `stored <key>, evicted <old>` |
| `GET <key>` | the value, or `miss` |
| `KEYS` | keys most-recent first, space-separated, or `empty` |
| `STATS` | `hits <h>, misses <m>` |

Before CAP: `error: no cache yet`. Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`.

milestones.title: Get and put without eviction
milestones.instructions: Implement `get` and the insert/update part of `put`, keeping `order_` (front = most recent) and `where_` in step.
hints: list::splice moves a node to the front in O(1) without invalidating iterators.
On an update, change the value in place and move the node to the front.

milestones.title: Eviction
milestones.instructions: When the cache is full and a new key arrives, remove the back of the list from both structures and return its key.
hints: Erase from where_ before pop_back, while you still have the key.
An update of an existing key never evicts.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
get and put are O(1): one hash lookup and list splices, no scans of the list; the two structures never disagree.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).

extensions: Make the cache thread-safe and explain the lock you chose.
